Definition: Extent to which the national digital identity system is integrated with the data exchange for identity verification and authentication
Comments: PGIBI (Civil and Criminal Integrated Management Platform) national biometric ID (BI Integrado with QR code/chip) launched 2017; ~30-39% coverage (2019-2020). BI platform allows interoperability with several public platforms including SIGFE, INSS, Investor Portal. ID4D Diagnostic (World Bank) confirms digital ID partially integrated into services. India-Angola DPI partnership (2025) to develop digital ID further.

Definition: Whether primary laws, acts, or legal instruments exist that establish authority for cross-government data sharing and govern the data exchange system
Comments: Presidential Decree 46/18 (2018) approved PNAGIA enabling cross-government data sharing. Law No. 22/11 (data protection) governs data processing and interconnection. LBTIC 2023-2027 mandates legislation on digital platform interoperability and security for public administration. Law No. 7/17 (Network/IT Systems Protection). Electronic signature implemented Jan 2023.

Definition: Extent to which the data exchange enables services accessible to all population groups including persons with disabilities, elderly, low literacy
Comments: Angola ranked 156th/193 on UN E-Government Development Index 2024 (score 0.4149, below African average 0.4247). Digital literacy gaps documented. ID card coverage only ~30-39%. Services centralized in Luanda. BI card processing dependent on physical offices. Significant accessibility barriers especially for rural/disabled populations.

Definition: Provisions ensuring national control over government data and protecting against unauthorized foreign access
Comments: Law No. 22/11 (data protection) requires APD authorization for data interconnection. National cloud platform (INFOSI) construction commenced 2025 to keep data in Angola. LBTIC 2023-2027 mandates data security standards. However enforcement noted as weak by CMS Expert Guide. Ratified AU Cybersecurity Convention 2019 but limited domestic enforcement capacity.

Comments: SIGFE (financial management) rolled out to 164 municipalities nationally but internet gaps in ~40% of municipalities. SEPE operates at national level. PNAGIA covers central and local state administration. Rural and remote area connectivity challenges well-documented. Partial subnational coverage.
